entry:gpai-cop:cov.note: All nine coverage elements are supported, timing included (trigger points in the Framework, full assessment before placing on the market). Measure 4.1 tiers are capability-based, measurable and set by signatories; the 10^25 FLOP presumption is the Act's. Commitment 6 (legal text Art. 55(1)) and Appendices 4.2–4.5 cover unreleased parameters, interfaces, physical access, insider threats, external security reviews and red-teaming. Measure 5.1 lists filtering, refusals and staged access; marking falls under the separate Art. 50 code. Model Report updates go to the AI Office at least every six months; non-signatories must justify alternative compliance.

entry:prep:desc.note: v2 (15 Apr 2025) is still the published version: three Tracked Categories with High/Critical thresholds, Research Categories (long-range autonomy, sandbagging, nuclear/radiological), persuasion out, low/medium dropped, model autonomy split; SAG recommends, Leadership decides, the board SSC oversees and can reverse; scalable evaluations before deployment plus deep dives; elicitation as a lower bound; High security standard (threat models, defence in depth, access management); safeguards for misuse and misalignment in Safeguards Reports; halt commitment for Critical; marginal-risk conditions; annual review. Astra (3 Sep 2026) is the first Critical cyber model; UK AISI, Apollo (Astra) and METR (GPT-5.6) evaluated. The FGF maps to SB 53 and the EU CoP and covers reporting to authorities; its May 2026 date rests on the PDF's Last-Modified header (openai.com announcement inaccessible).
